body:
Good morning, Kern County. It’s a warm September Tuesday, with temperatures at Meadows Field sitting at 64 degrees, a high near 91 on the way, and moderate air quality at 57. Police in Arvin have a new chief starting his first full week on the job, and crews spent the pre-dawn hours fighting a vegetation fire along the railroad tracks north of Highway 58.

## The Kern Overnight

The overnight hours kept first responders moving across the county. Just after 5 a.m., a vegetation fire along the Union Pacific Railroad tracks north of Highway 58 drew a full wildland assignment. Two engines, three patrol units, a water tender and two dozers were dispatched, along with multiple battalion chiefs, a division supervisor and a safety officer. A helicopter was placed on standby and air-to-ground coordination was requested, with additional strike-team resources held ready as crews worked to keep the flames from spreading. No injuries were reported, and the fire was knocked down before sunrise.

Earlier, around 12:09 a.m., a pursuit ran westbound along California Avenue with speeds called out from 60 to 95 miles per hour. Dispatchers noted light traffic and no pedestrians as the vehicle turned north and eventually pulled into a residence parking lot, where units moved in. Then at 2:11 a.m., a separate incident sent officers searching through a backyard and an attic after a pursuit ended at a home. One person was reported to be in the backyard, a second was last seen walking west, and a K-9 unit joined as officers fanned out on foot, checking spots where someone could hide.

In the river bottom, a brush fire burning in heavy grass and riparian vegetation was reported around 10:37 p.m. at roughly a quarter- to half-acre. The fire moved slowly, but crews had to figure out how to reach it, weighing access from the river side while requesting additional resources as the flames stayed in heavy fuels. Later, around 4:06 a.m., a semi truck went down in the number four lane of southbound Interstate 5; the driver was out placing warning triangles, and a second semi sat on the right shoulder while units called for a heavy-duty tow. Anyone heading down I-5 this morning should expect potential delays in that area.

The overnight log also included an armed robbery investigation at 10:15 p.m., with the victim describing a suspect in a green shirt, gray pants, green hat and white shoes. At 11:01 p.m., officers were sent to a convenience store parking lot for a man with an open alcohol container who was refusing to leave and harassing customers. A theft reported earlier at a Ming Avenue home improvement store was passed to patrol units with a suspect vehicle description and left pending for service, and at 11:38 p.m., deputies requested backup for a large gathering at a lake recreation area.

## Today's weather

Expect a mostly sunny day with a high near 91 degrees and a low around 64 overnight. It’s currently 64 at Meadows Field, with no active weather alerts and air quality at 57, which is moderate. That means it’s fine for most outdoor plans, though sensitive groups might want to take it easy this afternoon. There are no fires currently impacting the valley, and the breeze should stay light through the day.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that Arvin’s new police chief, Cecilio Velasco, hit the ground running on his first day Monday.** Velasco, a bilingual law enforcement veteran with 12 years of experience in Kern County, told the station his initial focus is listening to his officers and figuring out what the department needs, from resources and infrastructure to the tools required for community safety. He also addressed one of the department’s biggest challenges, officer retention, saying leadership, support and morale will be key to keeping officers committed to Arvin. Residents have previously shared their excitement about having a bilingual chief leading the department, and Velasco said he’s grateful for the warm welcome.

**According to Bakersfield Now, northbound Interstate 5 near the Grapevine was heavily impacted after multiple multi-vehicle crashes.** The report, which came from a headline, said drivers faced significant delays along the corridor and were urged to expect a slow commute. No details on injuries or how many vehicles were involved were available at the time of publication, but the crashes appeared to snarl traffic through the mountain section.

**KGET 17 reports that Cal State Bakersfield has opened an expanded, grocery-store-style food pantry called The Nest.** The 2,500-square-foot facility replaces a much smaller pantry that opened in 2017, and it came together after six years of planning and a student referendum. Everything inside is free, and the need is real: about 4 in 10 CSUB students, roughly 4,000 people, experience some level of food insecurity, according to Dr. Jason Watkins, director of the Essential Needs Resource Center. The pantry recorded more than 25,000 visits last year and distributes about 3,000 pounds of food each week during the semester, stocked through donations and a partnership with the Community Action Partnership of Kern.

**In a separate 23ABC report, a 33-year-old man has been arrested in connection with last week’s stabbing death outside the Target at Valley Plaza.** The victim, 20-year-old Aden Alejandro Aguila, was stabbed around 8 p.m. and died at Kern Medical about an hour later. According to the Bakersfield Police Department, Brett O’Leary was arrested Saturday on allegations of first-degree murder; a knife found near the scene is believed to be the weapon. Investigators say O’Leary and Aguila got into an altercation in the parking lot that briefly moved inside the store, and O’Leary is expected to be arraigned Tuesday.

**KGET 17 also announced that work is underway for the 2026 Bakersfield Christmas Parade.** The station shared the news without specific dates or route details yet, but organizers are already planning for the annual downtown tradition. It’s a reminder that even in September, the holidays aren’t as far away as they seem.

## Something good

There’s a bright spot on the CSUB campus this week: The Nest, the university’s new grocery-store-style food pantry, is open and free for students and staff. The expanded 2,500-square-foot space is the result of years of planning and a student referendum, and it’s already meeting a huge need — the pantry saw more than 25,000 visits last year and hands out roughly 3,000 pounds of food weekly. It’s the kind of resource that makes a real difference for the 4 in 10 students who face food insecurity.

And for those already thinking ahead to the holidays, organizers have started working on the 2026 Bakersfield Christmas Parade. It’s a beloved community tradition, and knowing plans are moving along is a cheerful thought for a warm September morning.

## Coming up this week

There are several chances to take part in local government over the next few days. On Tuesday, the Development Streamlining Ad Hoc Committee meets at noon, the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission follows at 2 p.m., and the Historic Preservation Commission convenes at 4 p.m. Wednesday brings a busy day at City Hall, with a City Council meeting starting at 3:30 p.m. and a second council session at 5:15 p.m. The Planning Commission meets Thursday at 5:30 p.m., and on Monday, Sept. 21, the Finance, Economic Development and Jobs Committee gets together at noon. The Homelessness Committee follows on Tuesday, Sept. 22, also at noon.

Over at the Fox Theater, the month is packed with entertainment. “It’s A 2000s Party: Bakersfield” takes over the stage Friday, Sept. 18, followed by “Cults & Classics: What Ever Happened to Baby Jane?” on Sept. 21. MEN I TRUST brings special guest Evan Wright on Sept. 23, MIKE SHERM performs Sept. 26, and “Cults & Classics: Young Frankenstein” rounds things out Oct. 5. Whether you’re into classic films or live music, there’s something to catch downtown.
